purpose: Apply the older JANUS A18 microkernel and Wave Rider architecture to Scout coordination so intake, admission, cohort formation, drain, evidence, health and memory remain narrow, replaceable and auditable.

microkernels.responsibility: Receive append-only peer messages and translate them into narrow task atoms without changing Scout identity.
Admit a bounded set of coordinated work claims; identical work may coalesce but every origin message and sender remains attached.
Seal bounded work waves before execution so routing decisions do not adapt to future result quality.
Close admission, let admitted work finish, preserve failures and defer overflow instead of deleting it.
After drain, classify workflow utility and observation routing without promoting workflow provenance to scientific truth.
Track fetch/query load, failures and degraded conditions as the Scout analogue of thermal/power health protection.
Require source URLs, fetch state and hashes where available; peer messages remain routing context, not empirical evidence.
Commit plans, traces, deferred work, failures and provenance into the append-only JANUS lineage and CAUSAL_ACK layers.

wave_policy.rationale: The current deterministic public discovery runner fetches at most eight source records per execution pass; sealing one eight-claim peer cohort keeps admission capacity aligned with observable execution while overflow survives for the next spiral turn.
